blocks.prompt: 7. [Prove by mathematical induction:] \(1 + nx \le (1 + x)^n\) for \(n \ge 2\) and \(x > -1\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh ek inequality hai jis mein \(x\) bhi hai; induction \(n\) par lagegi aur \(n = 2\) se shuru hogi (extended induction). Isay Bernoulli's inequality kehte hain.
Shart \(x > -1\) kyun? Is se \(1 + x\) positive rehta hai, aur positive number se multiply karne par inequality ka nishan nahi badalta.
Plan: base case mein \((1 + x)^2\) expand karna; hypothesis ko \(1 + x\) se multiply karna; aur extra term \(kx^2\) ko, jo kabhi negative nahi hoti, chhor dena.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(S(n): (1 + x)^n \ge 1 + nx\), jahan \(x > -1\) fix hai.
Saabit karna hai: \(S(n)\) har integer \(n \ge 2\) ke liye sahi hai.
Tareeqa: \(n\) par extended mathematical induction. \(x > -1\) ke dono taraf 1 jama karein to \(1 + x > 0\); yeh baat inductive step mein kaam aayegi.

Base case: \(n = 2\) rakhein
\[(1 + x)^2 = 1 + 2x + x^2\]
\[\ge 1 + 2x\]
Is liye \(S(2)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: Kisi bhi real number ka square kabhi negative nahi hota, \(x^2 \ge 0\). Is liye \(1 + 2x + x^2\) kam az kam \(1 + 2x\) ke barabar hai.

Induction hypothesis: \(S(k)\) ko sahi maan lein, \(k \ge 2\)
\[(1 + x)^k \ge 1 + kx \quad (A)\]
Kyun: Kisi integer \(k \ge 2\) par inequality ko sahi farz kiya.

Inductive step: (A) ko \(1 + x\) se multiply karein
\[(1 + x)^{k+1} = (1 + x)^k(1 + x)\]
\[\ge (1 + kx)(1 + x)\]
Kyun: \((1 + x)^{k+1}\) banane ke liye ek aur \((1 + x)\) chahiye tha. \(1 + x > 0\) hai, is liye (A) ke dono taraf is se multiply karne par nishan \(\ge\) wahi raha.
Dhyan dein: Agar \(x < -1\) hota to \(1 + x\) negative hota aur nishan ulat jata; isi liye shart \(x > -1\) zaroori hai.

Expand kar ke extra term chhorein
\[(1 + kx)(1 + x) = 1 + x + kx + kx^2\]
\[= 1 + (k + 1)x + kx^2\]
\[\ge 1 + (k + 1)x\]
Kyun: Term by term multiply kiya aur \(x + kx = (k + 1)x\) likha. \(k\) positive hai aur \(x^2 \ge 0\), is liye \(kx^2 \ge 0\). Ek non-negative term hata dene se baaqi cheez chhoti ya barabar rehti hai, is liye "\(\ge\)".

Nateeje jorein
\[(1 + x)^{k+1} \ge 1 + (k + 1)x\]
Is liye \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: Pichhle do qadam ek chain bana dete hain: \((1 + x)^{k+1} \ge (1 + kx)(1 + x) \ge 1 + (k + 1)x\).

Conclusion
\(S(2)\) sahi hai aur har \(k \ge 2\) par \(S(k)\) se \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hota hai. Principle of extended mathematical induction se \(1 + nx \le (1 + x)^n\) har integer \(n \ge 2\) aur har \(x > -1\) ke liye sahi hai.
Kyun: Induction ki dono sharten poori ho gayin.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 3,\ x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\)
\[(1 - \tfrac{1}{2})^3 = \tfrac{1}{8}\]
\[1 + 3(-\tfrac{1}{2}) = -\tfrac{1}{2} \le \tfrac{1}{8} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Negative \(x\) (jo \(-1\) se bara ho) par bhi inequality chalti hai. Yeh check is liye chuna ke students aksar sirf positive \(x\) par aazmate hain.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(1 + nx \le (1 + x)^n\) har integer \(n \ge 2\) aur \(x > -1\) ke liye.
